title: pwd
description: Print the full path of the current working directory.
notes: Useful as a sanity check inside scripts before running relative-path commands.

title: ls -la
description: List all files in a directory, including hidden dotfiles, with permissions, owner, size and mtime.
output:
drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Jul 20 09:11 .
-rw-r----- 1 syslog adm 20481 Jul 26 08:02 auth.log
notes: The leading dot entries (. and ..) are the current and parent directory.

title: cd
description: Change the current shell directory.
notes: 'cd -' returns to the previous directory; 'cd' alone goes to $HOME.

title: mkdir
description: Create a directory, with -p creating parent directories as needed.
notes: Combine with -m to set permissions at creation time, e.g. mkdir -m 700.

title: rm
description: Remove files or directories. -r is recursive, -f suppresses prompts.
notes: Irreversible — there is no Recycle Bin. Never run against a wildcard you have not previewed with ls first.

title: mv
description: Move or rename a file or directory.
notes: Overwrites the destination silently unless -i (interactive) is used.

title: cp
description: Copy files or directories. -r copies directories recursively, -p preserves attributes.
notes: Use rsync instead of cp for large trees or when resuming interrupted copies.

title: chmod
description: Change file permission bits, either numerically (750) or symbolically (u+x).
notes: Numeric mode: read=4, write=2, execute=1 summed per owner/group/other.

title: chown
description: Change the owning user and/or group of a file.
notes: Requires root or sudo unless changing your own files to a group you belong to.

title: find
description: Search a directory tree for files matching criteria (name, type, size, time, permissions).
notes: 'find / -perm -4000' is a classic first step for hunting SUID binaries during privilege-escalation review.

title: grep
description: Search file contents for a pattern. -r recurses, -n shows line numbers, -i ignores case.
output: auth.log:412:Jul 26 03:14:02 sshd[901]: Failed password for root
notes: -E enables extended regex; -v inverts the match; -c counts matching lines.

title: awk
description: Pattern-scanning and text-processing language, commonly used to extract columns.
notes: $0 is the whole line, $NF is the last field; -F sets the field separator.

title: sed
description: Stream editor for filtering and transforming text, most often used for find/replace.
notes: -i edits files in place; always test without -i first on production logs.

title: tar
description: Archive files, optionally with gzip (-z) or bzip2 (-j) compression.
notes: c=create, x=extract, t=list contents, v=verbose, f=filename (always last flag before the path).

title: zip / unzip
description: Create or extract .zip archives.
notes: unzip -l lists contents without extracting — use this first on unknown archives.

title: curl
description: Transfer data to/from a URL; -I fetches headers only, -o saves output, -s is silent.
notes: -k skips TLS verification (lab use only); -H adds a custom header.

title: wget
description: Non-interactive downloader for files over HTTP/HTTPS/FTP.
notes: --spider checks that a URL exists without downloading it.

title: ssh
description: Open a secure shell session to a remote host.
notes: -J chains through a jump host; ~/.ssh/config lets you alias hosts.

title: scp
description: Securely copy files between hosts over SSH.
notes: -r for directories; scp is deprecated in favor of rsync/sftp on newer OpenSSH but still widely used.

title: rsync
description: Efficiently synchronize files/directories, locally or over SSH, transferring only diffs.
notes: --delete mirrors deletions on the destination; -n does a dry run.

title: systemctl
description: Control and query systemd services (start, stop, restart, enable, status).
output:
● ssh.service - OpenBSD Secure Shell server
   Active: active (running)
notes: 'systemctl list-units --failed' quickly surfaces broken services.

title: journalctl
description: Query the systemd journal (logs).
notes: -f follows live like tail -f; -p err filters by priority.

title: iptables
description: List, add or remove packet filtering / NAT rules in the legacy netfilter table.
notes: Rules are evaluated top-down; put specific ACCEPT/DROP rules before broad ones.

title: ufw
description: Uncomplicated Firewall — a friendlier front end for iptables on Debian/Ubuntu.
example: ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 22
notes: 'ufw logging on' enables connection logging to syslog.

title: netstat
description: Show network connections, listening ports and the owning process (legacy, use ss instead).
notes: Deprecated on modern distros in favor of the iproute2 'ss' command.

title: ss
description: Modern replacement for netstat; dumps socket statistics.
notes: -s prints summary statistics; -o shows timer info for TIME-WAIT sockets.

title: dig
description: Query DNS servers for records (A, MX, TXT, etc).
notes: dig -x reverse-resolves an IP; dig @8.8.8.8 queries a specific resolver.

title: host
description: Simple DNS lookup utility.
output: example.com mail is handled by 10 mail.example.com.
notes: Lighter weight than dig; good for quick scripted lookups.

title: nslookup
description: Interactive/batch tool for querying DNS servers.
notes: Considered legacy compared to dig, but still present on nearly every system.

title: traceroute
description: Show the network path (hop by hop) packets take to a destination.
notes: Use tracepath as an unprivileged alternative; mtr combines ping+traceroute live.

title: tcpdump
description: Capture and display packets on the wire from the command line.
notes: -nn avoids DNS/port name resolution for speed; open the .pcap later in Wireshark.

title: crontab
description: Edit the current user's scheduled cron jobs.
notes: Fields are: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week command.

title: top
description: Live, updating view of running processes and system resource usage.
notes: Press 'k' to kill a PID from within top, 'q' to quit.

title: htop
description: Interactive, color process viewer — a friendlier top.
notes: Not installed by default on minimal images; apt install htop.

title: kill
description: Send a signal to a process, most commonly to terminate it.
notes: -9 (SIGKILL) is not catchable/ignorable; prefer -15 (SIGTERM) first for graceful shutdown.

title: ps
description: Snapshot of currently running processes.
notes: 'ps -ef --forest' shows the parent/child process tree.

title: history
description: Show the shell command history for the current user.
notes: HISTFILE controls where this is stored (~/.bash_history by default) — a key forensic artifact.

title: df
description: Report filesystem disk space usage in human-readable form.
output:
Filesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda1 40G 12G 26G 32% /
notes: Watch for 100% usage — many services fail silently on a full disk.

title: du
description: Estimate disk usage of files/directories. -s summarizes, -h is human-readable.
notes: Great for quickly finding what's eating disk space.

title: mount
description: Attach a filesystem to the directory tree; run with no args to list current mounts.
notes: -o ro,loop is the standard read-only, forensically-safe way to mount a disk image.

title: lsof
description: List open files, including network sockets held by processes.
notes: On Unix, 'everything is a file' — lsof also reveals which process is holding a deleted file open.

title: last
description: Show a listing of last logged-in users from /var/log/wtmp.
notes: 'lastb' shows failed login attempts from btmp; both are common brute-force indicators.

title: who / w
description: Show who is logged in and what they are doing.
output: USER TTY LOGIN@ IDLE JCPU PCPU WHAT
notes: 'who -b' shows the last system boot time.

title: uname
description: Print system information: kernel name, version, hostname and architecture.
notes: Combine with 'cat /etc/os-release' to identify the exact distro/version.

title: free
description: Display amount of free and used memory, human-readable.
output:
total used free shared buff/cache available
Mem: 15Gi 4.1Gi 2.0Gi
notes: 'available' is a better indicator of true free memory than 'free' alone.

title: useradd / usermod
description: Create (useradd) or modify (usermod) a local user account.
notes: -aG appends to a group; forgetting -a with -G overwrites all existing group memberships.

title: passwd
description: Change a user's password, or with -l/-u lock/unlock the account.
notes: Root can change any user's password; regular users can only change their own.

title: sudo -l
description: List the commands the current user is permitted to run via sudo.
output:
User analyst may run:
  (ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx
notes: A key privilege-escalation enumeration step — misconfigured NOPASSWD entries are a common finding.

title: visudo
description: Safely edit /etc/sudoers with syntax checking to prevent lockouts.
notes: Never edit /etc/sudoers directly with a text editor — a syntax error can lock out sudo entirely.

title: ssh-keygen
description: Generate a new SSH key pair.
notes: ed25519 is preferred over rsa for new keys — smaller and faster with equivalent security.

title: openssl
description: Swiss-army-knife for TLS certs, hashing and encryption from the shell.
notes: 'openssl x509 -noout -dates -in cert.pem' prints just validity dates — handy for cert-expiry checks.

title: gpg
description: Encrypt, decrypt, sign and verify files/messages using GnuPG.
notes: Use --armor for portable ASCII output instead of binary.

title: md5sum / sha256sum
description: Compute a cryptographic checksum of a file, used for integrity verification.
notes: Always prefer sha256 over md5 — md5 collisions are trivial to engineer.

title: file
description: Identify a file's type by inspecting its content/magic bytes, not its extension.
output: sample.exe: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows
notes: A quick, safe first step on unknown malware samples before deeper analysis.

title: strings
description: Extract printable character sequences from a binary file.
notes: -n sets minimum string length; often the fastest way to spot embedded URLs or IPs in malware.

title: stat
description: Show detailed file metadata: size, permissions, and MAC (modify/access/change) timestamps.
notes: Comparing Modify vs Change times can reveal timestamp tampering during an incident.

title: diff
description: Compare two files line by line and show differences.
notes: -u (unified) output is the format expected by 'patch'.

title: hexdump / xxd
description: Display a file's raw bytes in hexadecimal (and ASCII) form.
notes: '4d5a' at offset 0 is the 'MZ' magic bytes of a Windows PE executable.

title: base64
description: Encode/decode data in base64, often used to move binary data through text channels.
notes: -d decodes; attackers frequently base64-encode PowerShell/shell payloads to evade simple filters.

title: chattr / lsattr
description: Set/view extended ext2/3/4 filesystem attributes such as immutable (+i) or append-only (+a).
notes: Even root cannot modify an immutable file without first clearing the flag — a useful tamper-resistance control.

title: dd
description: Low-level block copy tool, used for raw disk imaging and wiping.
example: dd if=/dev/sdb of=evidence.img bs=4M status=progress conv=noerror,sync
notes: Double-check if=/of= before running — a swapped input/output can destroy data irrecoverably.

title: apt / dnf / yum
description: Install, update or remove software packages (Debian/Ubuntu apt, RHEL dnf/yum).
notes: 'apt-get changelog pkg' can help confirm whether a CVE fix is present in the installed version.

title: dpkg / rpm -qa
description: List installed packages (Debian dpkg / RHEL rpm), useful for software inventory during IR.
notes: Comparing package lists against a known-good baseline can reveal unauthorized installs.

title: nc (netcat)
description: Read/write data across network connections — used for banner grabbing, quick file transfer, or listeners.
notes: -z performs a fast port scan without sending data; extremely useful for connectivity troubleshooting.

title: auditctl / ausearch
description: Query the Linux audit framework logs for events matching a rule key, user, or syscall.
notes: 'auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k passwd_changes' watches a file for write/attribute changes.

title: lastlog
description: Show the most recent login for every user on the system.
output:
Username Port From Latest
analyst pts/0 10.0.0.7 Sat Jul 25 22:01:09 2026
notes: Accounts showing '**Never logged in**' but with a valid shell are worth investigating.

title: getfacl / setfacl
description: View or set POSIX Access Control Lists for finer-grained permissions than the standard rwx model.
notes: ACLs let you grant one extra user access without changing the file's primary group.

title: lsblk
description: List block devices (disks/partitions) in a tree view.
output:
NAME  FSTYPE  LABEL  MOUNTPOINT
sda
├─sda1 ext4          /
notes: -f additionally shows filesystem type and UUID — handy before mounting an unknown disk image.

title: ip a / ip route
description: Show or manipulate network interfaces, addresses and routing (modern replacement for ifconfig/route).
notes: 'ip -s link' adds interface traffic statistics (packets/bytes/errors).

title: watch
description: Run a command repeatedly, showing full-screen output — good for watching a value change live.
notes: Ctrl+C exits; -d highlights differences between successive updates.
